builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FairCompressAgent: An Agentic Framework for Fairness-Aware Model Compression for FPGA Deployment
summary: The method replaces manual, ad hoc selection and composition of pruning, quantization, and low-rank factorization configurations with a language-model planner that iterates over measured compression outcomes under explicit accuracy, fairness, and cost constraints. It costs an execution layer that runs repeated fine-tuning and evaluation per candidate configuration, plus planner API calls, which is feasible on a single GPU but adds engineering complexity beyond a fixed compression recipe. It can fail when the planner proposes unsatisfiable constraint combinations, when results from the single Fitzpatrick-17k/VGG-11 benchmark do not transfer to other models or tasks, and when the FPGA deployment target itself is irrelevant to teams serving via GPU or third-party APIs.
rationale: The constraint-driven search over composed compression methods is implementable on one 24 GB GPU, but evidence is limited to one dataset and one small model with modest fairness and storage gains, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot rather than direct adoption.
technique: Agent-guided fairness-aware compression pipeline for FPGA

claims.statement: The method replaces manual, ad hoc selection and composition of pruning, quantization, and low-rank factorization configurations with a language-model planner that iterates over measured compression outcomes under explicit accuracy, fairness, and cost constraints. It costs an execution layer that runs repeated fine-tuning and evaluation per candidate configuration, plus planner API calls, which is feasible on a single GPU but adds engineering complexity beyond a fixed compression recipe. It can fail when the planner proposes unsatisfiable constraint combinations, when results from the single Fitzpatrick-17k/VGG-11 benchmark do not transfer to other models or tasks, and when the FPGA deployment target itself is irrelevant to teams serving via GPU or third-party APIs.

Selected compressed model reduces inference tensor storage by 59.54% while validation average precision rises from 0.5141 to 0.5233 and equalized opportunity falls from 0.2251 to 0.2168; the agent reaches the same selection as one-shot planning with 7.33 versus 12 average candidate evaluations.
